title: Transitivity of derived tensor products under base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $R$-algebras, and put $T=A\otimes_R B$. For a commutative ring $\Lambda$, regard $\Lambda$ as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, so that complexes of $\Lambda$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], K-flat complexes and K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] (which exist [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]) and total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] apply, and write $D(\Lambda)$ for the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\Lambda$-modules. For complexes $E,K$ of $A$-modules put $E\otimes_A^{L}K=P_E\otimes_A K\in D(A)$, where $P_E\to E$ is a K-flat resolution over $A$, and $K\otimes_R^{L}B=K\otimes_R Q\in D(A)$, where $Q\to B$ is a K-flat resolution of $B$ over $R$ ($A$ acts through $K$; this object lives in $D(A)$, not in general in $D(T)$). Each $b\in B$ acts on $K\otimes_R^{L}B$ in $D(A)$ through the endomorphism of $B$ in $D(R)$ given by multiplication by $b$; with the action of $A$ this makes every $H^i(K\otimes_R^{L}B)$ a $T$-module. (1) There is an isomorphism $\alpha_{E,K}:(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B\cong E\otimes_A^{L}(K\otimes_R^{L}B)$ in $D(A)$, natural in $E$ and $K$, which commutes with the action of every $b\in B$ (on the right side through $K\otimes_R^{L}B$); hence each $H^i(\alpha_{E,K})$ is a $T$-linear isomorphism, and for every commutative $T$-algebra $C$ the maps $H^i(\alpha_{E,K})\otimes_T C$ are isomorphisms. (2) Let $C$ be a commutative $T$-algebra, $K'$ a complex of $C$-modules, and $\psi:K\otimes_A^{L}C\to K'$ a morphism in $D(C)$. Let $c_K:K\otimes_R^{L}B\to K\otimes_A^{L}C$ be the comparison morphism in $D(A)$ represented by $P_K\otimes_R Q\to P_K\otimes_R B=P_K\otimes_A T\to P_K\otimes_A C$ ($P_K\to K$ a K-flat resolution over $A$), and put $\varphi_K=\psi\circ c_K:K\otimes_R^{L}B\to K'$ in $D(A)$ ($K'$ regarded as a complex of $A$-modules). Then $\varphi_K$ commutes with the action of every $b\in B$ (acting on $K'$ through $B\to C$), so $H^i(\varphi_K)$ is $T$-linear and induces a $C$-linear map $\beta^i_K:H^i(K\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(K')$. For a complex $E$ of $A$-modules, $E\otimes_A^{L}K'=P_E\otimes_A K'$ is a complex of $C$-modules, isomorphic in $D(A)$ to $(E\otimes_A^{L}C)\otimes_C^{L}K'$ compatibly with the $C$-module structures on cohomology; let $\varphi_{E,K}=(1_E\otimes\varphi_K)\circ\alpha_{E,K}:(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B\to E\otimes_A^{L}K'$. Then $\varphi_{E,K}$ equals the composite of $c_{E\otimes_A^{L}K}$, the associativity isomorphism $(E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_A^{L}C\cong E\otimes_A^{L}(K\otimes_A^{L}C)$ and $1_E\otimes\psi$; it commutes with the action of $B$, so it induces $C$-linear maps $\beta^i_{E,K}:H^i((E\otimes_A^{L}K)\otimes_R^{L}B)\otimes_T C\to H^i(E\otimes_A^{L}K')$. If $C$ is flat over $T$ and $\beta^i_K$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, then $\beta^i_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and every complex $E$ of $A$-modules.

statement_change.what: restated in the D(A) form (R-dtt3144's recommendation) after three returns for an ill-typed statement (R-dtt3144, R-dtt0007, R-dtt0053): K (x)^L_R B and (E (x)^L_A K) (x)^L_R B are objects of D(A), not of D(A (x)_R B), unless A or B is R-flat, so the old derived tensor over A (x)_R B with C and the morphism K (x)^L_R B -> K' 'in D(C)' were undefined. New: (1) the D(A) isomorphism (E (x)^L_A K) (x)^L_R B = E (x)^L_A (K (x)^L_R B), natural in E, K, B-equivariant, so A (x)_R B-linear on H^i and compatible with H^i(-) (x)_{A(x)B} C for any C; (2) for a morphism psi: K (x)^L_A C -> K' in D(C), the comparison phi_K = psi o c_K and phi_{E,K} = (1_E (x) phi_K) o alpha_{E,K} (equal to the canonical map for E (x)^L_A K), and for C flat over A (x)_R B: if H^i(K (x)^L_R B) (x) C -> H^i(K') are isomorphisms for all i, so are H^i((E (x)^L_A K) (x)^L_R B) (x) C -> H^i(E (x)^L_A K') for every E. Exactly what the only citer lem-pc-rf-single-complex-inherited-tensor-condition step 2 uses.
statement_change.old_statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $R$-algebras, let $C$ be a commutative $(A\otimes_R B)$-algebra, let $E$ and $K$ be complexes of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let $K'$ be a complex of $C$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The canonical associativity and base-change isomorphisms in the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] identify the two complexes $((E\otimes_A^L K)\otimes_R^L B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}^L C$ and $(E\otimes_A^L(K\otimes_R^L B))\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}^L C$, naturally in $E$, $K$, and $C$; under this identification, tensoring any morphism $K\otimes_R^L B\to K'$ by $E$ gives the corresponding morphism from the first complex to $E\otimes_A^L K'$ (with all tensor products derived over the displayed rings).
